title: Blocking std::fs I/O inside async fn without spawn_blocking
description:
Synchronous filesystem calls run directly on the tokio runtime inside `async fn` bodies, stalling the reactor thread for the duration of the syscall.

persona-attestors/src/oidc.rs — `scan_token_caches()` (line 96) is a plain sync fn doing `std::fs::read_to_string` on up to three files (lines 106, 119) plus JSON parsing of each. It is called from three async trait methods: `enumerate()` (line 163), `prove()` (line 173), and `freshness()` (line 190). An Azure MSAL cache is routinely a few hundred KiB and lives on whatever the user's $HOME is mounted on — an NFS or autofs home hangs the whole runtime, not just this task. `prove()` and `freshness()` re-scan from disk on every call, so this is on the hot path.

persona-grpc/src/server.rs:18-32 — `async fn serve` calls `std::fs::remove_file`, `std::fs::create_dir_all`, and `std::fs::set_permissions`. One-shot at startup, so low impact, but `tokio::fs` is a drop-in here.

The rest of the crate already does this correctly: fido2.rs:64 wraps the blocking device enumeration in `spawn_blocking`, and gpg.rs:105 uses `tokio::process::Command`. oidc.rs is the outlier.

Fix: wrap `scan_token_caches()` in `tokio::task::spawn_blocking` at its three call sites (or make it async over `tokio::fs`), and switch server.rs to `tokio::fs`. Cheap `Path::exists()` probes (ssh.rs:35, tailscale.rs:29) are a single stat and can stay.
